name: Adnan Khashoggi

summary.text: Adnan Khashoggi (1935–2017) was a Saudi arms dealer and businessman. He acted as a middleman and financier in the 1985–86 U.S. arms sales to Iran that became the Iran-Contra affair, reportedly supplying about $25 million in bridge financing; documents released by a Senate subcommittee indicated that BCCI provided banking services to him in connection with those deals. He was arrested in Switzerland in 1988 in the Marcos case, extradited to the United States and acquitted with Imelda Marcos by a Manhattan federal jury on 2 July 1990.

facts.claim: A Manhattan federal jury acquitted Khashoggi and Imelda Marcos on all counts on 2 July 1990; the charges against Khashoggi had been reduced to obstruction of justice and mail fraud relating to helping the Marcoses conceal the purchase of four Manhattan buildings.
facts.quote: The jury acquitted former Philippines first lady Imelda Marcos and Saudi Arabian businessman Adnan Khashoggi on all counts in their racketeering and fraud trial

facts.claim: Khashoggi stopped fighting extradition from Switzerland after U.S. prosecutors reduced the charges and dropped the racketeering and conspiracy counts.
facts.quote: Khashoggi stopped fighting extradition when the US prosecutors reduced the charges to obstruction of justice and mail fraud and dropped the more serious charges of racketeering and conspiracy

facts.claim: Obituaries described Khashoggi as a middleman in the Iran-Contra affair who put together Iranian and Israeli arms dealers and provided $25 million in bridging finance for the arms sales.
facts.quote: Khashoggi put together Iranian and Israeli arms dealers and provided $25 million in bridging finance

facts.claim: Slate reported that Khashoggi brought the Iranian arms buyer Manucher Ghorbanifar into contact with the Israelis selling arms, provided bridge loans and lost roughly $10 million in the affair.
facts.quote: he brought Manucher Ghorbanifar, Iranian arms buyer, into contact with the arms-selling Israelis

facts.claim: A December 1986 press clipping in the CIA reading room, citing congressional committee sources, reported that about half of the $15.7 million put up by financiers led by Khashoggi vanished after being placed in Swiss accounts controlled by Oliver North and associates.
facts.quote: about half the $15.7 million put up by financiers led by Saudi Arabian billionaire Adnan Khashoggi vanished after being put into Swiss bank accounts controlled by North and his associates

facts.claim: Documents released by a Senate subcommittee indicated that BCCI provided banking services to Khashoggi in connection with the Iran-Contra arms deals; CIA official Richard Kerr said the agency was not involved in and had no knowledge of any use of BCCI for arms sales to Iran.
facts.quote: BCCI provided banking services to Saudi Arabian businessman Adnan Khashoggi in connection with the Iran-Contra affair

openQuestions: Site claim tested: Khashoggi as a BCCI 'insider'. Sources support that BCCI banked his Iran arms financing; nothing found shows him as a BCCI shareholder, officer or front man.

The Triad/Barrick connection (Khashoggi as an early investor alongside Peter Munk in the company that became Barrick) appeared only on advocacy and conspiracy sites in the search results and is not recorded; Barrick's own account of its 1983 founding does not mention him. The owner may wish to check 1980s business press or Barrick's early filings.
The Walsh final report's passages on Khashoggi were not located; the bridge-financing figures rest on obituaries and Slate.
The Senate BCCI report chapter cited (GlobalSecurity mirror) was listed in results but its Khashoggi passage was not quoted; the quote above is from the CIA reading-room clipping.
